question: In a separation by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) with elution with gradients:

options.opa: The composition of the mobile phase varies throughout the chromatography.
options.opb: The temperature of the mobile phase varies throughout the chromatography.
options.opc: The pressure of the mobile phase varies throughout the chromatography.
options.opd: The composition, temperature and pressure of the mobile phase are constant throughout the chromatography.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: The composition of the mobile phase affects the separation efficiency in HPLC -> Changing the composition of the mobile phase can alter the elution times of compounds -> Varying the composition of the mobile phase can improve resolution -> The composition of the mobile phase varies throughout the chromatography -> 80%

CHAIN: The temperature of the mobile phase influences the separation in HPLC -> Altering the temperature can impact the retention times of analytes -> Temperature changes can affect the selectivity of the separation -> The temperature of the mobile phase varies throughout the chromatography -> 75%

CHAIN: The pressure of the mobile phase plays a role in HPLC separation -> Adjusting the pressure can affect the flow rate and resolution -> Pressure changes can impact the efficiency of the separation -> The pressure of the mobile phase varies throughout the chromatography -> 70%

CHAIN: The composition, temperature, and pressure of the mobile phase are constant throughout the chromatography -> This scenario is unlikely in HPLC as variations in these parameters are often used to optimize separations -> 60%
